Thank you for sponsoring the WordPress Credits Program. This guide covers the page your company has on the Education Directory, how offers and codes reach students and mentors, what the program shows you and what it keeps to itself, and how a post you write is reviewed.

Signing in

Nobody registers on this site, and there is no sign-up form: the program makes every account for the person it belongs to. That means two things on your first visit:

  1. Go to the site's login page and use Lost your password? with the email address on your account. A reset link arrives at that address.
  2. Set a password, and you are in - unless your account also asks for a code, which the next part covers.

If the reset email never arrives, the address on your account is probably not the one you are checking. The login page cannot change it - ask whoever runs the program.

Signing in with a code

Besides your password, your account may ask for a code. Whether it does is the program's choice, and it is made for every account of your kind at once. When it does, there is nothing to set up first: from your next sign-in, the code arrives by email. When it does not, signing in works as described above, and a card on your page invites you to turn the code on for yourself.

After you enter your username and password, a second screen asks for the code. Which kind depends on how your account is set up.

An emailed code. The screen says a verification code has been sent to the email address on your account. The email comes from this site and has Login confirmation code in its subject line. It holds a code of eight digits. Type it into Verification Code and press Verify. A code works once, and for fifteen minutes. Resend Code sends a new one and the new one replaces the old, so use the newest email.

An authenticator app. If you have set one up, the screen asks for the code from your app instead: Authentication Code. Open the app, find this site in it, and type the six digits it shows. The digits change every 30 seconds, so type the ones on the screen at that moment.

A wrong code does not lock you out for good, but the site makes you wait a moment before the next try, and the wait grows with every wrong code, up to fifteen minutes. Wait it out, then type the code again, carefully.

Setting up an authenticator app

An app on your phone is quicker than waiting for an email, and it keeps working when your inbox does not. The card at the top of your page starts it. Its heading is Add a second step to your sign-in when the code is yours to choose, and Your account asks for a code when you sign in when the program asks for one; its button, Turn on two-factor authentication or Set up an authenticator app, opens your profile screen at its Two-Factor Options. Ignoring the card costs nothing: signing in keeps working the way it does now.

If you already use emailed codes and you open that screen more than about ten minutes after you signed in, it first asks you to confirm with Revalidate now, which takes one more code. Then follow the steps on the screen: install an authenticator app on your phone (any will do, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator), scan the QR code the screen shows with it, and type in the code your app then displays. Once the app is set up the card stops appearing.

Before you leave that screen, generate the recovery codes (the card calls them backup codes) and keep them somewhere other than your phone. Each works once, and the screen shows them only once. They are how you get back in if you lose the phone.

If you cannot get your code

  • The email does not come. Look in your spam folder, then press Resend Code. The email goes to the address on your account, so if you no longer read that mailbox, an emailed code cannot reach you.
  • Your phone or your app is gone. Under Having Problems? on the same screen, the site lists any other way your account has, for example Send a code to your email, or Use a recovery code if you saved some. Type one of your saved recovery codes where the screen asks for it, and cross that code off, because it will not work twice.
  • You have neither. Without the emailed code, the app or a recovery code, the site cannot tell that it is you, and it lets nobody past that screen. Tell whoever runs the program that you are locked out, and give them the username you sign in with. This guide cannot fix it for you.

Once you are signed in

Your page is drawn for whoever is signed in, so the same address shows each person their own page, and no change to a link shows anybody else's. The program's Administrators are the one exception: to help, they can open anyone's page, through a switcher only they are shown. A company's people share one Sponsor Dashboard, and an institution's people share one Institution Dashboard: everyone attached to the company or the institution sees the same page.

Your Sponsor Dashboard

Your company's page on the Education Directory is the Sponsor Dashboard, at /sponsor-dashboard/. You reach it after signing in with the account the program created for your company; every person the program attached to your company sees the same page. It opens with your company's name, logo and details, then At a glance, a row of tiles with your tier and what is waiting for your company, then the program's updates, its resources and your contact at the program, and under them your cards in four sections, Your sponsorship, What you offer, Mentors and Your company, in that order until your company arranges them. The header also names the contact person you gave the program, by name alone; the contact address is on the Company profile and logo card.

At a glance. The first tile is your tier, with the last day of its term and the days left in it, "ending today" on that day, the day the term ended once it has, or "no term"; it is there once the program has launched the sponsor tiers. After it comes one tile for each kind of thing that is waiting for your company, with a number and a line that says what waits: Offers returned with a note, Offers running low on codes (live offers with fewer codes left than the number you chose for the warning), Offers not switched on yet, Posts returned with a note, Event returned, Collaboration Agreement returned or Collaboration Agreement revoked, and Company profile details missing, which counts how many of the three details are empty. An offer is counted once, under the first of its three lines that fits it, so an offer an Administrator returned is never also counted as not switched on yet. A kind with nothing waiting has no tile, and when nothing at all waits, one dimmed tile says "Nothing waits for you". A tile that waits has a red edge at its start, and its line always says what waits, so the red is never the only sign. The tier tile waits too in the last thirty days of a term and once a term has ended; it always opens the Sponsorship card, where the card says how to renew. Press a tile with something waiting and the page takes you to the card that holds it, opened. The Event returned tile is there only while the Events card can show the note, which stands above the form that plans an event: from Champion up, with no event of yours still to take place, while your sponsorship is not paused and your term still has an event to plan. The figures that used to have tiles of their own, your next event, how many offers are live, how many mentors your company sponsors and your yearly reports, are on the lines of their cards.

Help. Under the tiles and above the cards, Program updates and announcements carries what the program publishes for sponsors, and Resources has this guide, the program's Slack channel and the Need help? button. Your contact at the program is under those buttons: the Administrator who looks after your company, with a link to write to them when the program has an address for them, and Book a call when it has a booking link. The page says "They look after your company's sponsorship. Write to them about anything the guide does not answer." The contact is there once the program has assigned an Administrator to your company, and only while that person still is one.

Arranging the page. Each section has two small arrows at its top right, named after it, for example "Move Your sponsorship up" and "Move Your sponsorship down". Press one and the section moves at once. The order is your company's, kept for everyone who signs in for it, and Your sponsorship comes first until somebody moves it. A section with nothing to show is left out and has no arrows: until the program has launched the sponsor tiers, Your sponsorship is not on the page.

The cards. A card folds and unfolds with one press on its title. The number beside a title is how many things it holds, and the words after it say where the card stands, so a folded card still tells you what is in it: "No event planned", "2 of 3 fields filled", "Accepted on September 3, 2026". Where a card has one thing to do, its button sits beside it: Plan an event, New offer, Edit, and Upload when the program has sent your agreement back or it is no longer in force, each of which opens the card at its top, the form in it; and Write a post, which opens the WordPress editor. A card's button shows while the card is folded; open it and the button gives way to the card. Sponsorship, Offers and codes and Mentors you sponsor are open when you arrive, and so is Events while an event of yours is still to take place; every other card stays folded until you open it, and after you send one of a card's forms the page comes back with that card open.

Your sponsorship. Sponsorship comes first: your tier and, when it has a term, the last day of that term; from Backer up, what your sponsorship funds; what your tier includes, as a checklist; and, below Partner, what the next tier adds. What each tier includes is what the program's partner page says for that level; above Friend, a line over the checklist says it comes with everything in the level below, for example "Everything in Backer, plus:". Its line says your tier with the term's last day and the days left in it. One press on Talk to your program contact tells them you would like to talk about the next tier. In the last thirty days of a term the card says how many days are left; from the day after the last day your company reads as a Friend, and the same button then asks your program contact to renew the term. The button keeps what you asked on record. Once the program's Partners page is published, the line with your tier links to it, at every level, since every partner is listed there in one alphabetical list; while a term runs the link follows the term's last day, and once a term has ended the line says so and asks for its renewal without it. At Friend the checklist says your company name is on the partner page. From Champion up, Events follows, with the events your tier includes and the planner for your co-hosted event; the paragraph after this one is about it. Reports follows once your program contact has finished your first yearly report: your yearly report of the program and of your sponsorship, one for each term - Open shows it in a new tab, ready to print, and PDF downloads the copy your program contact attached. Its line says how many yearly reports you have and which term the latest is for. Badge follows from Supporter up: the badge in its light and dark versions, and the embed code with a Copy button; the badge names your tier and the current year, and once a term has ended the year it ended, and its line says the same. The program's site serves the badge, so a change of tier shows on your Sponsor Dashboard at once and on your own site within an hour, with nothing to paste again.

Events lists the events your tier includes and holds the planner for one of them, your co-hosted webinar or event. It is open while an event of yours is still to take place, and its line names the soonest one, its day in your time zone and how many people have joined, or, until the program approves it, that it is waiting for the program; with none, it says "No event planned", and Plan an event beside it opens the card, where the form is, whenever you can plan one. The program plans the partners session, and for a Partner the launch communications, with you. You plan one event at a time and, while a term runs, one per term, or as many more as the program grants for that term, dated no later than the term's last day: the date and the start time, in your own time zone, which the form names; the length in minutes; the places, left blank for no limit; a title; a description, which the Partners page shows once the program approves the event, so the call link goes in its own box; and the call link, which only the people who join, and the program, see. A term's days are counted on the site's clock, so a start late on the term's last day in your own time zone can already fall on the next day there; the planner then names the last day and the site's time zone, for example "Choose a start on or before January 31, 2028, the last day of your sponsorship term on the site's clock (Europe / Warsaw)." When your term is renewed before it ends, the current term still runs to its last day and the renewed term starts the day after it; an event dated in the renewed term stays in it, and moving it earlier is refused in the same way, for example "Choose a start on or after February 1, 2027, the first day of your current sponsorship term on the site's clock (Europe / Warsaw)." When the program grants your term more events, the list says so under the co-hosted event, for example "and 2 more this term, granted by the program", and the form says how many your term allows, for example "Your term allows 3 events."; they count for that term alone, and a renewed term starts again from your tier's one. Plan the event sends it to your program contact, and nobody else sees it until an Administrator approves it. If the program returns it with a note instead, everyone who can sign in for your company is emailed the note, and it stands above the form when you plan again. Once it is approved, everyone who can sign in for your company is emailed a calendar file for it, and the event is listed for the program's students and mentors beside their calls, for Administrators on the Administrator Dashboard and for institution contacts on the Institution Dashboard, where each of them can join it or leave it. The Partners page lists it too, under Upcoming events, until it ends: its title, your company's name, its day and time in the site's time zone, its length and its description, with any address in it that starts with http://, https:// or mailto: taken out, and never the call link, the places or who joined; under the list, a visitor who is not signed in finds a Sign in to join button, and a student, mentor, institution contact or Administrator who is signed in a link to the page where they join it. Until it has taken place, Your event shows where it stands, "Waiting for the program's OK." or approved with how many people have joined, never who, with Change the event and Cancel the event. When Plan the event or Save the changes is refused for something you can put right, a detail missing or not valid, a start outside your term or one that has passed, fewer places than the people already on the event, another change to your company's events going through or a save that failed, the form comes back once with what you typed, Change the event drawn open when it was a change, and a value longer than its box allows comes back empty. A cancel, or a change of the date, the start time, the length, the title or the call link, emails everyone who joined, with a calendar file that updates the event or takes it off their calendar: the first fifty straight away and the rest within minutes, and the card says whether everyone who joined has been told or is being told. Everyone who can sign in for your company is emailed each change and cancel too, once the event was approved, and your program contact is told; a change of the description or the places alone reaches only them, and saving the form without changing anything emails nobody and says "Nothing changed." The day before your event, everyone who joined is emailed a reminder with the call link, and everyone who can sign in for your company one that says how many people have joined so far, never who; neither carries a calendar file. The reminders go out with the program's daily run, normally the day before the event, sometimes closer to it, and never twice: an event approved less than a day and a half before it starts may get none, and once they have gone out a change sends no second one, since its own email gives the new time. In the form's place the card then says "Your event for this term is planned already." while your term runs, or "Your next event can be planned once this one has taken place." if your sponsorship has no term, or when the program granted your term more events and another can still follow this one; once the event still to take place is the last your term holds, "Your events for this term are planned already."; and once your event for the term has taken place, "Your event for this term has taken place already.", or, once every event the program granted it has, "Your events for this term have taken place already.", for the rest of the term. A plan pressed anyway is refused in the same words. Each person who can sign in for your company has ten presses an hour across Plan the event, Save the changes and Cancel the event; the next one reads "Ten an hour is the limit. Try again in an hour." Past events lists the events that took place, each with its day and how many people joined. If your sponsorship stops including events - your term ends, your tier changes to one without them, or the program pauses your sponsorship - the card keeps an event of yours still to take place with Cancel the event alone, and an approved one reads "Approved, but no longer offered: your company's sponsorship does not include events at the moment."; nobody new can join it. With nothing still to take place, there is no Events card.

What you offer. Offers and codes is what your company gives the program's students and mentors: its line says how many of your offers are live, how many offers and changes wait for an Administrator's review while any do, and how many times they were claimed this month, and the card opens on the form for a new offer; the next section is about it. Usage counts, by month and by offer, how many people took an offer: a chart of the last twelve months, a table and a CSV to download, and its line counts every claim. Nobody is named there. Posts lists the posts your company wrote for the program's students and where each one stands; its line counts the published ones and the ones waiting for review, and while the card is folded Write a post sits beside it whenever you can write one. Posts start at Backer, so at Friend and Supporter the card is there only while your company has a post of its own, one from before the levels, one returned to you or one the program held back, and then says that your tier includes no posts. A post appears under your offer in Tools from our sponsors, on the Student Report Card and the Mentor Report Card, once an Administrator publishes it; the last section is about posts. To tell the program what more your company would like to do, write to your program contact, named under Your contact at the program, near the top of the page.

Mentors. Mentors you sponsor lists the mentors your company sponsors and how many students each one guides; its line counts them, or says "None yet". Mentors looking for a sponsor lists the active mentors who asked to be listed; one press tells your program contact you would like to sponsor one of them.

Your company. Company profile and logo is your company as the program records it: the details on the left, your logo on the right, and a line saying whether all three details are filled in: the website, the contact person and the contact email, anything else you would like to share being optional. What you save here is kept by the program, so keep it current; a logo in color and one in white for a dark background are shown wherever the program names you. Logos look alike side by side when they share a shape, so upload a horizontal one, about twice as wide as it is tall, at least 300 pixels wide (600 or more looks sharper), as a PNG, JPEG or WebP image, transparent where possible. From Supporter up, the profile also holds a Description for the partner page: a sentence or two about your company, 300 characters at most, shown with your logo and your name on the program's Partners page, where every partner is listed in the same format, in alphabetical order. A Friend is listed by name alone, so the box is not there, and a description saved while your company was a Supporter or above is kept but not shown. People lists everyone who can sign in for your company; ask your program contact to add or remove a person. Collaboration Agreement is where the agreement between your company and the program lives: download the text, upload the signed copy, and read where it stands (waiting for review, accepted, returned with a note, or out of force), which its line says too, with the day it was accepted.

Offers, codes and claims

An offer is something your company gives the program's participants: a license, a plan, a credit, a course seat, a discount. It is of one of two kinds. A pool of one-time codes is a list of codes you paste or upload, one per line or as a CSV; each code is handed to one person, once. One code or link everyone uses is a single code or checkout link that every eligible person sees.

Creating an offer. The New offer form sits on the left of the Offers and codes card. Give the offer a title, say what a person gets in a sentence or two, how to redeem it, and where to find more information. Choose the kind. For a pool, paste the codes or upload a .txt or .csv file; codes are stored encrypted and shown only to the person who claims one. Choose who else the offer is open to: current students always are; mentors and the program team are your choice. Set the number of codes at which the program should warn you that the pool is running low and, if the offer has a last day, that day. Press Create offer: the offer starts as a draft that nobody but you can see. Above the form, a line says that offers are separate from the tiers: as the program's partner page says, partners at any level may offer free access to their products, so your company may have any number of live offers, whatever its tier. Drafts are unlimited.

The review. An Administrator reads every offer before students and mentors see it, and a line above the New offer form says so. When a draft is ready, press Send for review: the offer is then Waiting for review, still seen by nobody but you, and Take it back makes it a draft again. An Administrator approves it, and it goes live, or returns it with a note, which reaches you by email and shows under the offer's state: change the offer, then send it for review again. Once an offer has been approved, a change to what students see of it, its title, what a person gets, how to redeem it, where to find more information and, for one code everyone uses, the code or link itself, is saved and waits for review too, while students and mentors go on seeing the offer as it was approved. The offer says so under its details, and Discard the changes drops what waits. An approved change takes the place of what students saw; a returned one stays under the offer's details with the note, until you change it again or discard it. Everything else takes effect at once, with no review: pausing, resuming and ending an offer, its last day, who it is open to, the number of codes the warning waits for, and voiding the codes nobody has claimed. While anything of yours waits, the card's line says how many offers and changes wait for review.

Adding codes. Codes you add to a draft, or to an offer waiting for review, go in at once and are read with the offer when it is reviewed. A draft the program made for you, such as your first offer, can be switched on with no review; once you add codes to it, it needs one like any other, and its Switch on becomes Send for review. Codes you add to an offer that has been approved, whether it is live, paused or dormant, wait for an Administrator's review, since a code can be a whole checkout link: Add codes says "Your codes were saved and wait for an Administrator's review. Until they are approved, nobody can claim them.", and the offer says how many codes you added wait, beside any change of yours that waits. Until they are approved, nobody is handed one, the counts of the offer, and of what students see as left, leave them out, and the warning that the pool is running low stays as it was. An approval puts them in the pool with any change that waits, as one decision. A return takes them out of the offer with its note, which reaches you by email and shows under the offer's details with how many codes were taken out: add them again, changed or not, to send them for review once more. Discard the changes takes them out too, at once. A code that waits is still in the offer for the repeat check, so it cannot be added twice, and it counts toward the 5,000 an offer holds. Void unclaimed codes leaves the codes that wait as they are, so you can void an old batch and add a new one in either order. Ending an offer takes the codes that wait for review on it out of the offer. Codes an Administrator adds for you go in at once. Offers that students could already see before the review began stay as they are.

Your offers. The offers you have sit on the right, under Active offers, each folded to its title, its state and a line of counts: for a pool, how many codes are available, claimed and void; for a shared code, how many people took it. Open one to edit it, to pause, resume or end it and, for a pool, to add codes or void the ones nobody has claimed. An offer that has ended, or whose last day has passed, moves under Ended and expired offers.

States. A draft is visible to nobody but you: send it for review when it is ready. An offer waiting for review is visible to nobody but you either, until an Administrator approves it. A live offer is shown to the people it is open to; the one live offer marked primary is the offer the program names as yours. A paused offer is hidden until you resume it, and its codes stay. A dormant offer is one the program held back while a tier capped live offers: it is hidden, its codes stay, the codes already claimed stay with the people who hold them, and you can end it but not resume it. No tier caps live offers now, so a dormant offer comes back by itself on the program's next daily run; one whose last day has passed stays as it is. An ended offer is over: nothing more can be claimed, it cannot be resumed, and the codes already claimed stay with the people who hold them.

Claims. A participant claims an offer from their own page: a student from the Student Report Card, a mentor from the Mentor Report Card, both in a section called Tools from our sponsors. For a pool, the program hands out the next available code, seals it to that person, and never shows it to anyone else, including you. When a pool falls below the number you set, the Offers and codes card says so and the program mails you once.

What you see. The Usage card counts claims by month and by offer: a chart of the last twelve months, a table with the totals, and a CSV of the same. Nobody is named there: the program keeps the list of who claimed which code, so that it can help a person whose code failed, and does not share it.

What your company can and cannot see

The Sponsor Dashboard shows your company its own things: its profile, its people, its agreement, its offers, its usage counts, its posts and its mentors. It never shows another sponsor's page, and it never shows who a student or a mentor is beyond what that person chose to make public. Once the program turns Sponsor tiers on, the Partners page lists your company by name at every tier, in alphabetical order with every other partner and in the same format, adding your logo, your website and your description from Supporter up; your badge, from Supporter up, names only the program, your tier and the year, with no logo or other company detail of its own.

  • Students. You see counts: how many students each of your mentors guides, how many people claimed an offer. You do not see names, addresses, reports, grades or the notes of a call. Your Reports card is the same: it names your mentors and counts, never a student.
  • Mentors. You see the mentors your company sponsors by name and WordPress.org profile, with how many students each one guides, and the active mentors who asked to be listed as looking for a sponsor. You do not see a mentor's calendar, notes or feedback.
  • Claims. You see numbers, by month and by offer. The program keeps the list of who claimed which code, so that it can help a person whose code failed, and does not share it with sponsors.
  • Events. You see how many people joined your co-hosted event, on the Events card, never who: the names are for Administrators alone, and no mail your company receives carries one; the reminder the day before your event says how many have joined so far, and nothing more about them. The call link you give reaches the people who join and the program, and no list shows it to anybody else. Your Reports card is the same: the yearly report lists the events held in the term with how many joined, and no names. Once the program approves your event, the Partners page lists it under Upcoming events until it ends, for anybody to read: its title, your company's name linked to your website, its day and time in the site's time zone, its length and its description, with any address in it that starts with http://, https:// or mailto: taken out; never the call link, the places or who joined. Under the list, a visitor who is not signed in finds a Sign in to join button, since the people the event is for join it on their own pages; a student, mentor, institution contact or Administrator who is signed in finds a link to that page instead, such as Join it on your Student Report Card, and anybody else who is signed in, such as someone who signs in only for your company, finds neither. An address written without http://, https:// or mailto:, such as an email address on its own or one starting with www., stays in the description as you wrote it. The event leaves the page if the program pauses your sponsorship or your sponsorship stops including events.
  • Records. The details you save on your profile card, your logo, the offer marked primary and what you send with Talk to your program contact are kept on this site, where Administrators read them.
  • The program's people. Administrators see your page as you see it, and can act on it for you: create an account for a colleague, record your agreement as on file, review a post. The switcher above the page, Viewing as sponsor, is theirs alone.

What you write on the dashboard is kept under the program's privacy policy, linked from the bottom of every page. Ask your program contact if you want something removed.

Posts, and how they are approved

From the Backer tier up, your company can write posts for the program's students, as the program's partner page says: a Backer one self-written educational post about the sponsored product, and a Champion or a Partner a second, with factual, value-neutral information about additional products. Posts are written in the site's editor. The Posts card on the Sponsor Dashboard has the Write a post button and lists every post your company wrote, with where each one stands.

Writing. A Backer has one post at a time, in review or published; a Champion or a Partner has two. Press Write a post, write in the editor, and submit the post for review. A post carries your company's byline and lands in your company's category, so readers know who wrote it. A post can carry images and links; it cannot carry code that runs on the page. When your tier includes no more posts right now, the Posts card says so where Write a post would be, and a post submitted anyway stays a draft. When your tier includes no posts at all, as at Friend and Supporter, the Posts card is on your Sponsor Dashboard only while your company has a post of its own (one from before the levels, one returned to you, or one the program held back), and says the same there, with the link to your posts in wp-admin, where you can still read them, edit a draft or a returned post and delete one. A post the program took off the site because your tier no longer includes it is dormant: the newest posts go first, the card says why, and a dormant post returns by itself when an Administrator sets a tier that includes it. If you edit a dormant post, it becomes a new submission, which an Administrator reviews before it is published again.

Review. Every post is read by an Administrator before it is published. The Administrator can publish it, or return it with a note that says what to change; a returned post comes back to you with the note on it, and you can submit it again. A published post appears to students and mentors under Guides from your company on your offer's card in their Tools section, and in the site's Sponsors category, which only signed-in participants can read.

Rules. Posts are for the program's participants: useful to a student learning WordPress, honest about what your product does, free of pricing pressure. The program's licensing and trademark rules apply to what a post says and links to. A post that reads as an advertisement is returned.

If posting is switched off for your company, the Posts card says so; ask your program contact.
